source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Data Canopy's Lithia Springs campus is a documented 10 MW of IT capacity, which is a real but mid-scale compute footprint rather than a hyperscale one.

The operator publishes 10 MW and 19,500 square feet of technical space, but no rack count, accelerator count, or power density. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 10 MW is roughly 250 racks. At 10 kW per rack it is about 1,000 racks. The square footage does not settle which applies, because 250 racks implies about 78 square feet per rack, a plausible hall, while 1,000 racks implies under 20 square feet per rack, which is tight for training gear.

The only published certification is LEED. That is a green building rating and says nothing about power redundancy, cooling topology, or network paths. It does not establish whether the campus can host high-density training racks, and no such specification is published.

Georgia has 49 mapped facilities, and this campus ranks third by published megawattage among the five in the state that publish a figure. Those five total 76.3 MW, so this campus is about 13 percent of the state's published capacity. Most Georgia facilities publish no figure at all, so the published total is a floor, not a full accounting of the state's data center load. The binding constraint on AI scaling here is the grid, not the building.
